📈US Stocks - Rotation Rotation Rotation 📉

I was recently asked "why is risk on when the S&P500 is below the 50SMA".
I pay little attention to the $SPY or the $QQQ since these are cap-weighted indices that skew the data significantly. The $DIA is price weighted (and also of little-to-no interest).

If you look at the one-week performance of $QQQ (pic1), you will see that money is flowing out of the largest companies - the MAG7 etc. Most of the map is red and negative.

However, if you zoom out and take a look at the entire market for the week, you can see plenty of health and strength in healthcare, biotech, airlines, utilities, diagnostics & research. This is clear rotation from high beta tech giants into other industries namely more defensive stocks - Healthcare and Utilities are breaking out of their Darvas Boxes.
You may consider some of these too risky (biotech) or too slow (low ATR like consumer staples) but that does not change that there are bullish industries in the market. The increase in oil flowing through the strait is reducing the cost of fuel which is positive for airlines and cruising as they enter their busiest season in the northern hemisphere. 

I pay (slightly) more attention to the equal-weight $RSP and $QQQE but really I focus on the entire equally weighted universe of $1B market cap and above, which would be closer to say the $IWM,  which is at new all-time highs.

It is certainly hard for the $QQQ and even $SPY to go to new ATH when its largest stocks are rolling over and maybe they lead the market lower but, from a pure data perspective, the overall equal-weighted market is bullish - you just have to fish where the fish are 🎣
Otherwise, enjoy some time off and wait for the eventual rotation back to the megacaps.










Vin @ The99th Percentile Fund (@99thPercentileX)
